summary: Lists supported requires statements: #Requires -Module and -Version, #AnsibleRequires -PowerShell, -CSharpUtil, -OSVersion and -Become (runs as SYSTEM if no become user), plus collection, relative and -Optional imports for AnsibleRequires.
questions: How do I require a minimum PowerShell version in a module?
How can a Windows module force become to get around WinRM limits?
How do I require a minimum Windows OS build?
Can I make a module util import optional?

answer_card.title: PowerShell requires statements
answer_card.answer_md:
- `#Requires -Module Ansible.ModuleUtils.<x>` (2.4)
- `#Requires -Version x.y` (2.5)
- `#AnsibleRequires -PowerShell <util>` (2.8)
- `#AnsibleRequires -CSharpUtil <util>` (2.8)
- `#AnsibleRequires -OSVersion x.y` (2.5, from `[Environment]::OSVersion.Version`)
- `#AnsibleRequires -Become` (2.5; runs with become, `SYSTEM` if no `ansible_become_user`)

`-PowerShell`/`-CSharpUtil` also support collection utils (2.9), relative names (2.10) and `-Optional` (2.12).
